To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the underpricing of A-shares IPOs is positively associated with the time between the offering and listing, the number of stock market investors in the province, and the number of shares issued, and negatively related with the underpricing of the B-share IPOs, while the long-term performance is negative for A-shares and positive for B-shares.
A-share IPOs are significantly underpriced and B-share IPOs are not; A-shares significantly underperform the market while B-shares significantly outperform the market in the long run.
A-shares are underpriced, B-shares are not, A-shares underperform the market in the long term, and B-shares outperformed the market.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the underpricing and performance of A- as well as B-share IPOs in the China market.
the underpricing and performance of A- versus B- share IPOs issued in China.
the long-run performance of IPOs and their underpricing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the underpricing of A- and/or B-share IPOs is not a signal of the future performance.
the Chinese stock market is inefficient.
A-shares underperform in the long term, while B-shares overperform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the underpricing of A-shares and the long-term performance of both A- and B-shares are related to the characteristics of the IPO firms, and the long-term underperformance of A-shares is due to their overvaluation at the offering date.
the A-share IPOs are underpriced and underperform, but B-share IPOs are not.
A-share IPOs are underpriced and underperform in the long run, while B-share IPOs are not underpriced and outperform in the long term.
The main takeaway from our work is that
underpricing and long-run performance of A-share IPO firms are related to the number and type of stock investors in a province, and the number of shares issued.
the Chinese government’s policy of allowing foreigners to buy B-shares has led to more efficient pricing of IPOs in the Chinese equity market.
the underpricing of A- and of B-share IPO is not due to the same factors, and that the long-term performance of the two types of shares is different.
